messages:
Elaine: Quick proposal — I sketched a 'satellite modules consolidation' playbook for long-lived feature adapters. Aim is to reduce duplicated adapters across services and create a small runtime shim we can roll out incrementally. Sharing the draft below.

Jonah: nice. can you paste the high-level steps?

Elaine: Sure — TL;DR: 1) identify canonical adapters (owner + tests), 2) add compat shims in sources, 3) introduce feature-flagged routing to canonical service, 4) migrate consumers in waves, 5) remove old code after 2 successful waves + perf/err checks.

Sam: what do you mean by "compat shims" — runtime libs or http adapter layer?

Elaine: small runtime shim lib (Go) that implements the old adapter interface and proxies to the canonical endpoint. no DB rewrite during migration. shim lives in repo: infra/sat-shims.

Kai: can we avoid cross-team deploy coordination by using a routing layer change instead? i.e. route at the ingress to canonical service when flag on per-tenant basis.

Elaine: yes — routing-layer toggle is the plan for wave-0. the shim is fallback for teams that can't toggle quickly.

Jonah: risk callouts? rolling back if canonical service regresses?

Elaine: rollback strategy: flip routing back to original service, or enable shim fallback (shim -> old code path). need automated smoke test for each tenant wave.

Sam: can we automate smoke tests with existing e2e infra? I can add new test tags.

Sam: quick draft of smoke check: ```
# smoke-check pseudo
curl -sS -X POST https://staging-routing/api/v1/route-check -d '{"tenant":"t-123","payload":"small"}' | jq '.status=="ok"'```

Kai: also add metric: per-tenant 5xx rate and latency (p50/p95) for both routes for 1h after cutover. if 5xx > 0.5% or p95 regressed >20% rollback.

Elaine: agreed. We'll add alerts in console: route.migration.<team>.<tenant>.errors and .p95. ops-bot will create the alert during the rollout job.

ops-bot: created alert draft: route.migration.alerts/elaine-2026-03 (internal link).

Jonah: timeline? I suggest pilot with 3 non-critical tenants first, then 2-week pause, then expand. total ~6 weeks depending on team bandwidth.

Sam: owners? which team will own canonical adapter and SLAs?

Elaine: proposal: Platform (runtime team) owns the canonical adapter library and infra; Consumer teams own integration and migration. Platform provides compatibility guarantee for 1 major and 1 minor interface change during 6 months.

Kai: are we versioning the adapter API? semver?

Elaine: yes — semver for the shim interface. Migrations that require breaking changes must follow the rollout + opt-in major version switch.

Jonah: DB migrations — any stateful adapters we need to worry about?

Elaine: trying to avoid state moves. for a few adapters that persist, plan is: dual-write (canonical + old) behind a feature-flag for 2 waves, then backfill read-path to canonical, then switch. add data integrity checks: row counts/hash comparison.

Sam: can we add a lightweight integrity query: `SELECT count(*) FROM legacy WHERE migrated_at IS NOT NULL` and compare with canonical? I can add that to rollout job.

Elaine: perfect. add margin tolerance 0.1% for eventual consistency.

Kai: tooling to track progress across all consumers? a simple spreadsheet is fine, but we should expose a dashboard with tenant statuses. devx-bot can create a PR to add status endpoints.

devx-bot: created ticket INF-4823: "sat-modules migration dashboard" assigned to DevX.

Jonah: blockers: 1) some teams hard-code adapter paths in lambda bundles, 2) tests rely on local adapters. Both need short spikes.

Elaine: I'll run a spike with infra to list hard-coded usages (grep across repos) and produce a remediation sheet.

Sam: okay to start pilot next Monday if infra spike wraps this week.

Kai: thumbs up from me. please post final playbook in /docs/arch and add the checklist there.

Elaine: will do. final playbook link once uploaded. thanks all :thumbsup:
